newsitem.title: UK: POLL-SBC Warburg come top overall in Extel Survey.
newsitem.headline: POLL-SBC Warburg come top overall in Extel Survey.

text.p: SBC Warburg toppled NatWest Securities to take top place in the all sectors league of the 1997 Extel Survey of investment analysts on Wednesday.

SBC Warburg, whose five year winning streak ended last year with a drop to third place, led this year by a comfortable margin. NatWest Securities slipped to second slot while Merrill Lynch leapt to third place from sixth last year.
In the UK sectors league, SBC Warburg again stole first place from NatWest Securities, who moved to second position.

After last year's gain in votes, HSBC James Capel lost ground and dropped from second place in 1996 to fifth in the 1997 all sectors league. UBS Ltd retained its fourth position, with BZW dropping to sixth from fifth place last year.

Dresdner Kleinwort Benson stayed at seventh and ABN AMRO Hoare Govett kept eighth place in the league. Goldman Sachs International regained votes and moved back to ninth, with Morgan Stanley International slipping to tenth position.

The league table for research of pan-European industry sectors, including Britain, ranked NatWest first with a relatively strong lead, ahead of SBC Warburg and Merrill Lynch. This was weighted by funds under management and market capitalisation.

In the European continent sectors league, SBC Warburg again ranked top, and with a much bigger margin. NatWest Securities moved back into second place ousting UBS Ltd, ranked second in 1995, into fourth place. Goldman Sachs International jumped to third from seventh place in 1996.

For the fourth year running, the 1997 "All Stars" rating for the top ranked UK team went to Fergus MacLeod's "Oil, Integrated" team at NatWest Securities. HSBC James Capel's pharmaceutical analysts, led by Andrew Tivenan, won the top ranked European sector team weighted by market capitalisation.
The top votes for an individual analyst again went to Fergus MacLeod, covering oils for NatWest. Runner up was Charles Burrows who covers the engineering sectors for HSBC James Capel.

Assessments of broker services favoured NatWest Securities for overall quality of research but Merrill Lynch showed the best improvement in research during the last year. Merrill Lynch also topped the overall quality ratings for sales and execution.

The 1997 Extel survey shows the rankings of the top research brokers and their analysts weighted by size of funds under management by the respondents who voted for them. The league tables are based on the weighted results, which again are close, with only 2.3 percent of the votes separating the top five brokers and 80 percent of votes going to the top eight brokers in the all sectors league.
The survey showed that 51 percent of the respondents found pan-European research of "some importance" to them, up from 39 percent last year.
A total 45 percent of respondents increased the amount of research they are doing in-house and 51 percent said they plan to increase it over the next year.

The survey is based on the opinions of 105 fund managers responsible for almost 70 percent of domestic investment in the UK equity market. The 61 percent response rate included 71 percent of those managing funds of over 20 billion stg.
